summary: McNairy County, Tennessee sheriff Buford Pusser, celebrated as the crime-fighting hero of Walking Tall, ran a violent, self-serving war on the State Line Mob and is now believed to have murdered his wife in 1967 and staged it as a mob ambush.

evidence.note: born December 1937 on a farm in McNairy County, Tennessee
Phenix City crackdown pushes gangsters to the Tennessee-Mississippi state line
Jack and Louise Hathcock introduced as leaders of the State Line Mob
December 1959 marriage, then fence-post ambush of W.O. Hathcock Jr. starts the feud
returns to Adamsville after 1961 and becomes police chief, then constable and sheriff
deliberately cultivates a press myth, carrying a hickory stick on raids
1966 raid in which he kills Louise Hathcock, family says she was shot in the back
evidence that he killed his wife Pauline and faked the 1967 ambush
TBI reopens the cold case in 2022, exhumation and new autopsy in 2024
1971 book and 1973 film Walking Tall make him a national celebrity
dies in a sports car crash in August 1974

notes: covered_span runs to 2024 because the TBI reopening (2022) and exhumation (2024) investigate his own crime and get several minutes; a 2004 self-published book by ex-sheriff Mike Elam is also discussed. Birth years of Louise Hathcock and Pauline Pusser not given (Pauline was 33 in 1967). Mississippi side of the state line is also a setting but Tennessee dominates, so only US-TN is listed.
